messages:
sara (Support): Escalation from acme-marketing: 'streams silently stop after reconnect' but this time observed in multiple SDKs (py & go) not just node. Customer notes it behaves differently depending on client event-loop.

maria (Customer Success): How widespread? Any accounts on dedicated? They'll want SLA implications.

sara (Support): Only reported by them so far. Affects hosted API. They reproduced locally on three runtimes: Node 20, Python 3.11 (uvloop), Go 1.21. Repro pattern: start SSE stream -> network interruption (tcp fin) -> SDK auto-reconnect -> client receives a truncated final chunk and iterator exits without raising error. No server 5xx.

tyler (sdk-team): Can you get exact SDK versions? We've had changes recently to the async iterator state machine in py-sdk 0.10.0 and go-sdk 0.9.4.

sara (Support): Python sdk==0.10.0, Node redwood-js v2.3.2-canary (customer tried canary), Go redwood-go v0.9.4. They tried downgrading python to 0.9.8 and it behaved fine.

sara (Support): customer log (python) snippet:
```
INFO stream: open session=ses_9c2a
INFO stream: delta: "The product launch will be"
INFO stream: delta: " delayed due to supply"
// network blip simulated
WARN stream: reconnecting session=ses_9c2a resume_token=rt_7f
INFO stream: resume ok, got 200
INFO iterator: received final event type=done
// application receives StopAsyncIteration with incomplete text
```

aj (eng-runtime): Our edge logs for ses_9c2a show resume request hit runtime and we delivered all deltas. I see full sequence on server side. This suggests client-side loss during resume processing.

tyler (sdk-team): possible race in py async iterator where the resume handler sets generator.closed=true before buffering remaining events if resume race occurs with EOF. Also recent change to buffer flush on heartbeat could cause early termination.

sara (Support): customer also showed traces where they rotated API keys mid-test and one resume attempt got 401 then subsequent resumes worked. Not constant but happened once per 20 runs.

billing-bot: Alert: unusual token usage spike for account acme-marketing at 2026-01-21T02:12:45Z.

maria (Customer Success): They flagged billing concern 10x token spike during retries. Need mitigation to avoid double-charging if possible.

tyler (sdk-team): Short-term guidance to customer: pin SDK to the last known-good (python 0.9.8 / go 0.9.2) OR set RW_STREAM_RESUME_STRICT=1 to disable the new aggressive flush on resume (this env var will be in 0.10.1 rc). Also ask them to send a stable session_id (metadata) so server-side dedup can ignore repeated tokenized chunks.

sara (Support): Customer asked if we can provide a patched wheel for python. They can test quickly.

tyler (sdk-team): I'll cut a 0.10.1-rc1 wheel with an explicit ack-before-yield on resume and a regression test that simulates TCP RST mid-stream. Will post sha and pip link. Also adding guard so iterator does not raise StopAsyncIteration until we've seen a 'complete' or explicit timeout.

aj (eng-runtime): I'll enable a short-lived debug flag on edge for their account to capture raw SSE frame boundaries and resume token echoes. Link to logs will be shared privately.

sara (Support): Customer wants ETA. Can you give rough times? They need to decide whether to pause prod.

tyler (sdk-team): Repro + unit test: today. RC build + upload: within 6 hours. Customer test feedback: within 24h. If RC passes we'll cut patch release 0.10.1.

maria (Customer Success): Good. I'll relay timeline and request access to the debug logs. Also asking legal about credits for token overage if it looks like our client caused repeated billing.

// customer provided a small repro for Python 
// they used aiohttp SSE eventsource and an async-iterator wrapper
```
async for chunk in client.stream_async(prompt='x'*1000, session_id='acct-123'):
    print(chunk.text)
    await asyncio.sleep(0)  # yields control
```
// they trigger a network flake via iptables drop.
```


sara (Support): Notes: in Go they reported the iterator's Next() returned (nil, nil) once then closed. In Node they saw 'stream closed' event without 'done' message. All SDKs share a common protocol handler; likely bug introduced in resume token handling in runtime or client lib.

tyler (sdk-team): Action items (sdk):
- reproduce across py/node/go with the provided iptables-based flapper
- add integration tests that assert no partial final outputs after reconnect
- publish 0.10.1-rc (py) and 2.3.3-canary (node) and 0.9.5-rc (go) with ack-before-emit and auth-cache guards

aj (eng-runtime): Action items (runtime):
- verify resume handler returns full event stream when resume token provided
- instrument edge to log x-rw-resume and resume-token-body pairing
- look for any transient 401 on resume that could be auth-caching on lb

maria (Customer Success): I'll coordinate a scheduled test window with the customer tomorrow at 0900 PST. Please have RC links and steps ready.

sara (Support): I've opened INC-2026-0120-02 and attached customer logs. Will update when rc is published.

deploy-bot: Incident assigned: INC-2026-0120-02 -> tyler (sdk-team), aj (eng-runtime).
